scenes.title: One payment. Three emails.
scenes.label: MAYA'S CHECKOUT
scenes.voice: Maya pays one hundred and twenty dollars once. Her bank confirms one transaction. Then three order confirmation emails arrive, and the warehouse receives repeated shipping requests.
scenes.note: Repeated notifications do not prove repeated charges.

cues.text: Maya pays one hundred and twenty dollars once.
Her bank confirms one transaction.
Then three order confirmation emails arrive, and the
warehouse receives repeated shipping requests.

scenes.title: The acknowledgement was lost
scenes.label: WHAT WENT WRONG?
scenes.voice: The payment provider sends a signed success webhook. Our server processes it, but its acknowledgement is lost. The provider cannot tell whether processing finished.
scenes.note: A lost reply does not undo the database commit.

cues.text: The payment provider sends a signed success webhook.
Our server processes it, but its acknowledgement is
lost.
The provider cannot tell whether processing finished.

scenes.title: Retry repeats the unsafe work
scenes.label: SAME EVENT, AGAIN
scenes.voice: The provider retries the same event. An unsafe handler sends another email and shipment request. The webhook reports an existing payment. It does not charge the customer again.
scenes.note: One charge · three deliveries · repeated fulfillment intents

The webhook reports an existing payment.
It does not charge the customer again.

scenes.title: First protection: durable inbox
scenes.label: VERIFY, THEN ACCEPT
scenes.voice: First, verify the original request bytes, timestamp and merchant. Save the event identity in a durable PostgreSQL inbox. A repeated delivery is safely acknowledged without creating new work.
scenes.note: Inbox = durable delivery deduplication across restarts and replicas.

cues.text: First, verify the original request bytes, timestamp and
merchant.
Save the event identity in a durable PostgreSQL
inbox.
A repeated delivery is safely acknowledged without creating
new work.

scenes.title: Second: guard the payment state
scenes.label: NEW ID, SAME PAYMENT
scenes.voice: A different event identifier can still describe the same payment. Transition pending to succeeded only once. A late success notification must never move a refunded payment back to succeeded.
scenes.note: Delivery identity and business identity are different protections.

cues.text: A different event identifier can still describe the
same payment.
Transition pending to succeeded only once.
A late success notification must never move a
refunded payment back to succeeded.

scenes.title: Third: commit a reliable intent
scenes.label: OUTBOX + DESTINATION KEYS
scenes.voice: Commit the inbox, payment update and outbox intent in one database transaction, then acknowledge. A separate worker retries with stable email and fulfillment keys. Downstream systems must deduplicate too.
scenes.note: No external network calls inside the acceptance transaction.

cues.text: Commit the inbox, payment update and outbox intent
in one database transaction, then acknowledge.
A separate worker retries with stable email and
fulfillment keys.
Downstream systems must deduplicate too.

scenes.title: One payment. One logical outcome.
scenes.label: CUSTOMER PROTECTED
scenes.voice: Now repeated webhooks receive a safe acknowledgement without repeating the business action. One payment, one logical confirmation, one fulfillment intent. Monitor failures and reconcile ambiguous outcomes. These are illustrative counts, not production measurements.
scenes.note: Outbox intent alone is not exactly-once physical delivery.
